subject: physics_2
question_text: Write the colour code of a carbon resistor of resistance 23 kilo ohms.

verification.note: The mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. For this Paper-II bank the two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers. Physics hand-checked: 23 kΩ = 23 × 10³ Ω; digit 2 = Red, digit 3 = Orange, multiplier 10³ = Orange; code Red, Orange, Orange — matches the book.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Split into digits and multiplier
lines: Write the resistance as two digits times a
steps.margin_note: First mark. Force the number into the form (two digits) × 10ⁿ before touching colours.
steps.why: The code has exactly two digit bands, so the value must first be written as a two-digit number times a power of ten. 23 × 10³ is that form; 2300 × 10 is not.
common_mistakes: Writing 23000 Ω and trying to read colours from five digits.
Using 2.3 × 10⁴ — the code needs TWO digits before the multiplier, so use 23 × 10³.

recall.must_convey: That 23 kilo ohm is written as 23 times 10 cubed ohm, giving digits 2 and 3 with multiplier 10 cubed.
accept: two digits then the power of ten

steps.memory_tip: Always reshape to two digits × 10ⁿ first — the code cannot say three digits.

steps.label: The colour code
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Three bands in order: digit, digit, multiplier.
steps.why: Each number 0 to 9 owns one colour; 2 is Red and 3 is Orange, and the multiplier band reuses the same digit-to-colour table for the power of ten.
common_mistakes: Swapping the band order to Orange, Red, Orange — the digits must come in the order 2 then 3.

recall.must_convey: That the code is red, orange, orange — 2 is red, 3 is orange, and the multiplier 10 cubed is orange again.

steps.memory_tip: 3 and 10³ are the same colour here — Orange twice at the end.

insider_note: The working (23 × 10³) earns a mark on its own — jumping straight to Red, Orange, Orange risks losing it.
